relationships.subject: Capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: topical capsaicin stimulates the TRPV1 receptor on neurons, leading to the opening of ion channels and causing positive cation influx including Na+ and Ca+

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1-mediated calcium ion influx induces calpain, in turn causing axonal ablation and functional defunctionalisation in the PNS

relationships.subject: Capsaicin
relationships.evidence_quote: It inhibits specific voltage-gated sodium channels (VGSC) in the trigeminal ganglion neuron and prefrontal cortex pyramidal neurons

relationships.subject: MAPK pathway
relationships.evidence_quote: The activation of MAPK pathways causes the release of neurotransmitters CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide), substance P, and neurotrophin BDNF

key_findings: Review: topical capsaicin analgesia is attributed to TRPV1-mediated Ca2+ influx, calpain activation and axonal defunctionalisation; CNS effects remain uncertain.
Capsaicin may cause central hypersensitisation via MAPK-driven CGRP/substance P/BDNF release or inhibit VGSCs.
